name: Kerala infinite series for an arc
description: A Kerala mathematical tradition described an infinite series for computing an arc, interpretable in modern terms as an arctangent series.

date.label: Around 1550
date.basis: The cited historical account supports Around 1550; this is a dated documented episode, not proof of global priority.

events.statement: Jyesthadeva’s Malayalam Yuktibhasa described a series attributed in the tradition to Madhava.

evidence.locator: Biography, paragraphs on lost works and Yuktibhasa
evidence.supports: Later Kerala tradition records series attributed to Madhava; Yuktibhasa is dated approximately 1550.

contributions.resource: Authored the later Yuktibhasa account describing the series; not asserted to have invented it.

evidence.locator: Biography, paragraphs on lost works and Yuktibhasa
evidence.supports: Attributes Yuktibhasa to Jyesthadeva and reports his description of a series attributed to Madhava.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode established by the evidence collected here for this scoped achievement, not a claim of absolute priority.

caveats: Madhava’s mathematical writings are lost; attribution and an earlier date rest on later testimony. The approximately 1550 date is for the later description, not a dated original manuscript or proven date of discovery.

research.note: Independent check of MacTutor’s quotation and modern series interpretation; Jyesthadeva is author of the account, not asserted inventor. Event contributions, concept, places and extended measure scope were added in a later pass and have not been independently reviewed.

places.note: Kerala mathematical tradition in southwestern India; no exact place of composition asserted.
